title: Defining the clinical benefits of disease-modifying therapy in people living with spinal muscular atrophy who require permanent ventilation: a UK-based modified Delphi consensus process
abstract: Background: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare inherited neuromuscular disorder that may require permanent ventilation (PV) in severe cases. Although disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) have transformed outcomes for many, prior to this research, access in the UK was restricted for patients receiving PV (SMA-PV). This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations on DMT use and to define clinical benefit in SMA-PV. Methods: A multidisciplinary UK-based expert panel conducted a modified Delphi consensus process between 08 April and 09 June 2025. Draft statements informed by published evidence and expert insights were anonymously voted on for up to three rounds, with consensus defined as ≥75% agreement. Statements not achieving consensus were revised and re-evaluated. Input from a non-voting patient advisory panel (PAP) was also considered. The study was not prospectively registered. Findings: Excluding the Chair, 18 participants evaluated 22 statements across seven thematic areas specific to SMA-PV: DMT access; treatment initiation; treatment monitoring; defining clinical benefit; functional outcomes; quality of life (QoL); and future research priorities. All 22 statements achieved consensus after two voting rounds (100% participation; agreement range 89-100%). Two statements were revised and re-voted in round 2: one after narrowly missing consensus (72% agreement) and the other to incorporate PAP feedback despite achieving 100% agreement in round 1. The panel agreed that PV alone should not preclude access to DMTs and that trial access with personalised treatment goals may be appropriate. The panel also emphasised broader definitions of clinical benefit, including subtle changes in function and QoL, alongside sensitive assessment approaches and harmonised outcome measurement. Interpretation: These consensus-based recommendations support careful reconsideration of treatment exclusions for patients with SMA-PV and more inclusive, patient-centred approaches to evaluating treatment benefit. Funding: Roche Products Ltd.

title: Low-dose prednisolone and B vitamins for post-COVID-19 syndrome in Germany: the PreVitaCOV randomised clinical trial
abstract: Background: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is burdensome and not yet adequately treatable, with persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnoea, and cognitive impairment. The Pan American Health Organisation recommends rigorous evaluation of potentially beneficial interventions. We investigated the efficacy and safety of prednisolone and vitamins B1, B6, and B12 in patients with post-COVID-19. Methods: This randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (2 × 2 factorial design) was conducted in adults with post-COVID-19 at three university sites in Germany. Adult patients with persistent symptoms after a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection ≥12 weeks ago and without acute COVID-19, major comorbidities, pregnancy or breastfeeding, prior intensive care treatment for COVID-19, recent use of trial drugs, or potentially interacting concomitant medications were included. From January 13, 2023 until July 25, 2024 participants were randomly assigned to 28 days of once-daily oral treatment with prednisolone (20 mg on days 1-5, 5 mg on days 6-28), B vitamins (thiamine nitrate [B1], 100 mg, pyridoxine hydrochloride [B6] 50 mg, and cyanocobalamin [B12] 500 μg), prednisolone and B vitamins, or placebo. The primary outcome was change in overall symptom severity from baseline to day 28, assessed in the intention-to-treat population (participants who received at least one dose of study drug) at the first follow-up visit after randomisation with a customised Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) total T-score. A change of ≥3 points was considered clinically meaningful. Efficacy was assessed using a pre-specified factorial analysis of the main effects of prednisolone and B vitamins. Safety was assessed by analysing frequency and severity of adverse events in all randomised patients (safety population). This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05638633). Findings: Of 2498 patients assessed for eligibility, 323 were randomised and 310 patients had evaluable data for the outcomes. The mean age was 44 (standard deviation (SD) 13) years, 200 participants were women. The mean change in PROMIS T-score was -4·3 (SD 5·1) with prednisolone, -3·2 (SD 5·0) with B vitamins, -4·5 (SD 4·5) with prednisolone plus B vitamins, and -2·9 (SD 4·6) with placebo. The adjusted mean difference between participants treated with prednisolone and those not treated was -1·4 points (95% confidence interval (CI), -2·5 to -0·4; p = 0·008), driven primarily by the change in the fatigue subscore (-6·4 points, p < 0·001). B vitamins showed no statistically significant or clinically meaningful difference compared with no B vitamins (adjusted mean difference (MD), -0·1 points; 95% CI, -1·2 to +1·0; p = 0·85). Adverse events were equally distributed between groups, with no study-drug-related serious adverse events. Interpretation: This trial showed a statistically significant short-term reduction in symptom severity in the five dimensions of the PROMIS score in patients with post-COVID with low-dose prednisolone. However, the effect did not reach the prespecified threshold for clinical relevance. Further research is needed to confirm the efficacy of prednisolone and to determine the optimal dose and treatment duration while balancing benefits against longer-term adverse effects. Funding: German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, Vogel Stiftung Dr. Eckernkamp, Hevert-Arzneimittel GmbH & Co. KG.

title: Paediatric chronic hepatitis C and the global elimination gap: burden and trends from 1990 to 2023 in the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background: Paediatric chronic hepatitis C (PCHC) is often asymptomatic and underdiagnosed, and its contemporary global burden remains incompletely characterised. We estimated global, national, and socioeconomic trends in PCHC using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates, and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related liver cancer as a limited Supplementary analysis. Methods: We analysed GBD 2023 estimates of prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for PCHC in people younger than 20 years from 1990 to 2023. Results were summarised globally, across seven official GBD super-regions, and for 204 countries and territories using annual point estimates and supplied 95% uncertainty intervals. Because HCV-related liver cancer estimates were unavailable for children younger than 10 years, analyses of this endpoint were restricted to ages 10-19 years. Findings: Global PCHC prevalence was 0.380% (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 0.314-0.452) in 2023, representing a decline from 0.443% (0.376-0.514) in 1990, with an absolute change of -0.062 percentage points and a relative change of -14.1%. Mortality declined from 0.0890 (0.0504-0.1538) to 0.0595 (0.0303-0.1023) deaths per 100,000 population younger than 20 years, and the DALY rate declined from 7.49 (4.36-12.92) to 5.06 (2.62-8.40) per 100,000. The highest prevalences clustered in Central Asia, South-East Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa. Interpretation: The PCHC burden has declined globally, particularly mortality and DALYs, but prevalence has fallen only modestly. The continued high burden in Central Asia, South-East Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa, and marked country heterogeneity highlight the need to integrate antenatal screening, follow-up of perinatally exposed infants, and access to curative treatment for children aged 3 years or older into hepatitis elimination programmes in order to reach the 2030 elimination targets. Funding: National Institutes of Health.

title: Camrelizumab plus famitinib as first-line treatment for locally advanced or metastatic pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinomas (CAPSTONE): a multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial
abstract: Background: The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antiangiogenic agents has demonstrated a synergistic antitumor effect in numerous solid tumors, but has rarely been investigated in pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC). We assessed the activity and safety of camrelizumab (a programmed cell death-1 inhibitor) plus famitinib (an antiangiogenic agent) in patients with PSC. Methods: CAPSTONE is an open-label, single-arm, Simon two-stage, phase 2 trial done at eight sites in China. Eligible patients were aged between 18 and 75 years and had previously untreated stage IIIB-IV pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1, and at least one measurable lesion as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Patients received intravenous camrelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks and oral famitinib 20 mg once daily until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate (ORR) as per RECIST version 1.1 in the full analysis set, which included all patients who received at least one dose of study drug. Safety was assessed in all as-treated patients. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04888429, and enrollment is complete. Findings: Between August 4, 2021 and March 21, 2024, 28 patients were enrolled. With a median follow-up of 18.1 months, the confirmed ORR was 42.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 24.5-62.8). The disease control rate was 85.7% (95% CI 67.3-96.0). The median duration of response was 16.0 months (95% CI 5.0-29.9); the median progression-free survival was 7.1 months (95% CI 3.5-12.5); and the median overall survival was 18.1 months (95% CI 10.3-28.1). Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) of grade 3 or more were observed in 10 (35.7%) patients, the most common being decreased platelet count (four [14.3%]) and decreased neutrophil count (three [10.7%]). Three (10.7%) patients discontinued camrelizumab, and three (10.7%) discontinued famitinib due to TRAEs. Two patients died of unknown cause, which were assessed by the investigator as possibly related to study treatment. Interpretation: Camrelizumab plus famitinib showed antitumor activity in patients with locally advanced or metastatic PSC. This combination may be a potential first-line option for this patient population, and warrants further investigation in a large-sample trial. Funding: National Science and Technology Major Project of the Ministry of Science and Technology of China (No. 2024ZD0519700), National Natural Science Foundation of China (62131009, 82472969), Innovation Research Group Program of the Natural Science Foundation of Hubei Province (2026AFA036), Hubei Provincial Health Science and Technology Innovation and Achievement Transformation Project, Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd.

title: The lungs in Alström syndrome: a retrospective analysis
abstract: Background: Alström syndrome (AS) is a rare multisystemic disorder frequently associated with respiratory complications, which are a major cause of premature death. While fibrosis in multiple organs has been historically suggested as a hallmark of AS, including the lungs, definitive evidence in adult patients remains limited. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients diagnosed as AS seen in our National Multidisciplianry AS clinic from 2010 to 2024. Lung function test and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax was performed in a subset of patients. Postmortem lung tissue analysis was available from four patients. Findings: A total of 25/41 (61%) of the patients were unable to complete full lung function testing. Among those who did, 67% exhibited reduced lung volumes, with 47% showing decreased diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide but normal or elevated transfer coefficient for carbon monoxide, indicating extrapulmonary restrictive physiology. HRCT scans in 39 patients showed no evidence of diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis; however, breathing artefacts were common. Historical infantile cardiomyopathy was identified as a risk factor for adult pulmonary dysfunction. Post-mortem pathology reports were obtained from four patients and no diffuse fibrosis in the lung tissue was identified in any of the patients. Pulmonary hypertension and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome were identified as potential causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality, despite the absence of intrinsic interstitial lung disease. Interpretation: This is the first large cohort study to depict the lung in adult patients with AS. This study provides no evidence for diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis in adult patients with AS, challenging prior assumptions. Pulmonary dysfunction appears mainly due to extrapulmonary restrictive physiology, with infantile cardiomyopathy as a possible risk factor. Pulmonary hypertension and acute respiratory distress syndrome, rather than intrinsic lung disease, likely underlie respiratory morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for focused cardiopulmonary care. Although this study represents one of the largest single-centre cohorts of patients with AS reported to date, the overall sample size remains limited due to the ultra-rare nature of the disease and findings should be interpreted with caution. Funding: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

title: World cancer congress 2026
Risk of a statistical blind spot: the dangers of data shortages
abstract: Health-care optimisation depends on population-level statistics. Disease incidence, mortality, fertility rates, vaccination coverage, intervention uptake, and indicators of health inequities are some examples of measures that governments depend on when it comes to policy and decision making, determining where resources are allocated and whether interventions work. Data collection and processing require huge effort across surveys, censuses, administration records, registries, and statistical systems.

title: Efficacy and safety of oxfendazole in adults with Trichuris spp. infection in Pemba Island, Tanzania: a double-blind, phase 2a, randomised controlled trial
abstract: Background Trichuriasis caused by the intestinal parasites Trichuris trichiura and Trichuris incognita, remains a major public health problem. The widely used benzimidazoles albendazole and mebendazole show low efficacy, highlighting that more effective treatments are needed. One promising candidate is oxfendazole, a highly effective anthelminthic that is widely used in veterinary medicine. Within eWHORM, an adaptive basket trial platform for neglected helminth infections was set up to evaluate the safety and efficacy of oxfendazole against, among others, trichuriasis. Methods In this double-blind, phase 2a, randomised, placebo-controlled trial conducted between April 29 and July 16, 2025, on Pemba Island, Tanzania, we evaluated the safety and efficacy of oxfendazole against Trichuris spp. infection in adults aged 18–65 years. A total of 127 participants were randomised in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive either placebo on three consecutive days, 400 mg oxfendazole on day 1 followed by placebo on two consecutive days, 800 mg oxfendazole on day 1 followed by placebo on two consecutive days or 800 mg oxfendazole on three consecutive days. The primary outcome was Trichuris spp. egg count at day 18, expressed as eggs per gram of stool based on quadruplicate Kato-Katz thick smears. Secondary outcomes included cure rates and egg reduction rates for Trichuris spp., Ascaris lumbricoides , and hookworm. Adverse events were recorded 3 h, 24 h, and 18 days post-treatment. The trial is registered at the Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202412611774752). Findings Between April 29 and May 21, 2025, 229 participants were screened for Trichuris spp. infection, of whom 127 were treated. Of these, 31 received 3 × 800 mg oxfendazole, 34 received 1 × 800 mg oxfendazole, 30 received 1 × 400 mg oxfendazole and 32 received placebo. The egg count at day 18 was 1099.2 (SD 3354.6) for placebo, 218.3 (SD 506.4) for 1 × 400 mg oxfendazole, 148.4 (SD 244.7) for 1 × 800 mg oxfendazole and 36.2 (SD 117.5) for 3 × 800 mg oxfendazole. Cure rate for 3 × 800 mg oxfendazole was 75.9% (95% CI 57.9–87.8). Single oxfendazole doses revealed lower cure rates of 31.0% (95% CI 17.3–49.2) at 400 mg and 35.3% (95% CI 21.5–52.1) at 800 mg. The placebo group had a cure rate of 20.0% (95% CI 9.5–37.3). All doses were well tolerated and showed a similar number of adverse events compared to placebo. The most common adverse event was abdominal pain. Interpretation Single doses of oxfendazole showed no benefit over the cure rates reported in the literature for the currently used drugs albendazole and mebendazole against Trichuris spp. infections. However, given its high efficacy when used at multiple doses, the drug could play a role in targeted treatment schemes. Moreover, multiple-dose administration of oxfendazole may confer an ancillary public health benefit against Trichuris spp. when used to treat helminth infections requiring multi-day regimens, particularly in co-endemic regions. Funding EDCTP3 Joint Undertaking and the Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI).

title: Radiosensitising strategies in locally advanced head and neck cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RADIANCE-NMA)
abstract: Background Radiosensitiser enhance radiotherapy efficacy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Although cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy is the standard-of-care, over two dozen radiosensitising strategies have been evaluated in randomised trials with no network meta-analysis comparing all drug classes. Methods PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 26 June 2026 for Phase IIb–III randomised controlled trials evaluating concurrent radiosensitiser therapy in adults with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (nasopharyngeal carcinoma excluded). Studies lacking overall survival data and induction-only comparisons were excluded. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS). All treatment-effect estimates are reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Risk of bias in individual trials was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias (RoB 2) tool and confidence in the network estimates using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework. Random-effects network meta-analysis was done with frequentist (netmeta) and Bayesian (gemtc) frameworks. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified using the I 2 statistic and τ 2 ; publication bias and small-study effects were assessed using comparison-adjusted funnel plots and Egger's regression test. This study is registered with the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/cygsh). Findings A total of 44 trials (13,768 patients; 84% male) were included in the primary analysis, with 23 additional trials in sensitivity analyses (67 total; 19,527 patients). Risk of bias showed some concerns in 39 of 44 (89%) primary trials on the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Four treatments showed significant overall survival (OS) benefit versus radiotherapy alone: cisplatin plus 5-fluorouracil (hazard ratio (HR) 0.35; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.18–0.66), nimotuzumab plus weekly cisplatin (0.48; 0.29–0.81), weekly cisplatin (0.57; 0.44–0.74), and three-weekly cisplatin (0.79; 0.65–0.95). In the network estimate, weekly cisplatin was favoured over three-weekly (HR 0.73; 0.58–0.93); the underlying randomised trials were designed as non-inferiority comparisons. Between-study heterogeneity was moderate (I 2 = 48.9%; τ 2 = 0.036; Cochran Q=37.15, df=19, p=0.008), with no detected inconsistency (design-by-treatment global test p=0.88). The comparison-adjusted funnel plot and Egger's regression test showed no evidence of small-study effects, but are interpreted as exploratory given fewer than ten trials per edge on most comparisons. Grade 3–4 toxicity was highest with weekly cisplatin (pooled 71.6% across contributing trials) and lowest with immunotherapy combinations. Meta-regression confirmed enrolment era as a significant effect modifier (β = 0.23 post-2005 versus pre-2005; p=0.010), consistent with the transition from two-dimensional or conformal radiotherapy in earlier trials to intensity-modulated radiotherapy in modern trials. Interpretation Platinum-based multi-agent chemoradiotherapy and weekly cisplatin are the most effective radiosensitising strategies for locally advanced HNSCC. Weekly cisplatin appears at least non-inferior to the widely used three-weekly schedule and may be favoured in network-integrated estimates, though confidence intervals do not exclude clinical equivalence. Neither cetuximab-based regimens (with radiotherapy or added to chemoradiotherapy) nor immune-checkpoint inhibitors added to cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy significantly improved survival beyond standard cisplatin chemoradiotherapy. These findings provide a unified evidence framework for treatment selection and trial design. Funding None.

title: Efficacy and safety of intrathecal chemotherapy in leptomeningeal disease: a global retrospective multicenter analysis and review of the literature
abstract: Background Leptomeningeal disease (LMD) is a devastating complication of cancer with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. It affects approximately 5–15% of patients with solid or hematopoietic malignancies. The optimal route of chemotherapy delivery for LMD patients remains controversial, with intrathecal administration theoretically offering direct access to the central nervous system. The effectiveness and safety of intrathecal chemotherapy (ITC) remain contentious, and most previous studies have been limited to small sample sizes. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of ITC in LMD patients using global data. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data from the International Collaborative TriNetX Network, comparing outcomes among patients with LMD across cancer types who received ITC plus systemic chemotherapy versus systemic chemotherapy alone. The study included all cancer types across 106 healthcare organizations, encompassing more than 156 million patients. The analysis was conducted on August 12, 2025, and eligible index events were restricted by the TriNetX platform to the preceding 20 years (August 12, 2005, through August 12, 2025). After including all cancer patients with LMD of both sexes aged between 18 and 90 years, we first excluded patients who received radiotherapy to the central nervous system. Second, 2311 subjects who received systemic chemotherapy alone and 292 subjects who received ITC plus systemic chemotherapy were included and compared using multivariate Cox regression to calculate hazard ratios (HRs). Third, propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using age, sex, primary cancer type, treatment interventions, and baseline laboratory values at diagnosis. This yielded 247 cases in each cohort, which were compared using univariate survival analysis with HRs. The primary outcome of both the univariate and multivariate analyses was all-cause mortality at multiple time points. Secondary outcomes included chemotherapy-related adverse effects, meningitis, hydrocephalus, cognitive-communication deficits, seizures, sepsis, and hypotension following treatment. A subanalysis was also performed to assess the isolated efficacy and safety of specific ITCs (in combination with systemic chemotherapy), such as methotrexate and cytarabine, compared with systemic chemotherapy alone. Finally, we conducted a literature review from inception through December 2025 to identify all prospective phase 2 and 3 clinical trials that evaluated the efficacy and safety of ITC in patients with LMD. Findings We found that the predominant cases receiving ITC were of hematopoietic and lymphoid origin (176 patients; 71.3% in ITC vs. 173; 70% in controls), followed by breast, lung, and melanoma primary cancers (48 [19.4%], 21 [8.5%], and 17 [6.9%] in ITC vs. 59 [23.9%], 20 [8.1%], and 14 [5.7%], respectively). Multivariate Cox regression analysis revealed a significant reduction in 30-day mortality associated with ITC (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.26–0.76; p=0.003). At 90 days, the association with mortality did not reach statistical significance (HR = 0.75; 95% CI, 0.55–1.02; p=0.066). By 180 days, mortality rates did not differ between cohorts (HR = 0.93; 95% CI, 0.73–1.20; p=0.58). One-year univariate survival analysis post-PSM indicated worse survival with ITC (HR = 1.34; 95% CI, 1.01–1.78; p=0.04). Over the follow-up period, patients receiving ITC experienced higher rates of adverse events, including meningitis (36.8% vs. 21.5%; HR 1.94; p < 0.001), hydrocephalus at 30 days (8.5% vs. 4.0%; HR 3.04; p=0.01), and cognitive communication deficits (26.3% vs. 16.2%; HR 1.75; p=0.01). Interpretation This large-scale study provides important insights into the role of ITC in both solid and hematologic malignancies. Although the overall findings did not demonstrate a long-term survival benefit, ITC was associated with improved 30-day survival (HR = 0.4; p < 0.05). No difference was observed at 90 days, and beyond that time, an inverse effect emerged, possibly reflecting treatment-related toxicities and cancer-related complications. Given that survival in LMD typically ranges from 4 to 16 weeks and rarely exceeds 6 months, these results suggest that ITC provides a short-term survival advantage but may not alter, or may worsen, longer-term outcomes with a significant increase in chemotherapy adverse events, hydrocephalus, meningitis, and communicative cognitive impairment. Funding None.

title: Prenatal exposure to acrylamide and neuropsychiatric disorders: a biomarker-based birth cohort study with 34 years of follow-up
abstract: Background The widespread exposure to acrylamide from diet and tobacco smoke during prenatal development is of concern as acrylamide is neurotoxic and potentially contributes to the development of neuropsychiatric disorders. We aimed to examine associations between prenatal acrylamide exposure and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Methods In this biomarker-based study of offspring from the Danish Foetal Origins 1988–1989 birth cohort, pregnant women were enrolled at gestational week 30 at a routine antenatal clinic at Aarhus Hospital, Denmark. Liveborn singletons with available exposure and outcome data were included. The current study was conducted from 2022 to 2026. Prenatal acrylamide exposure was quantified using haemoglobin adducts (HbAA) in maternal blood collected during pregnancy. Incident cases of depression, anxiety, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), co-occurring ADHD and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), as a composite outcome, and any neuropsychiatric disorders were identified from national diagnostic and prescription registries in the first 34 years of life (1988–2023). The associations were estimated using adjusted log-linear Poisson regression models. Findings Among 861 offspring, 146 cases of depression, 72 of anxiety, 45 of ADHD, 53 of co-occurring ADHD and ASD, and 150 cases of any neuropsychiatric diagnosis occurred during follow-up. Median (P5–P95) HbAA was 93 (45–250) pmol/g Hb and maternal active smoking during pregnancy was common (42%). Each 10-pmol/g Hb increase in HbAA was associated with IRRs of 1.02 (95% CI 0.99–1.05) for depression and 1.03 (0.99–1.07) for anxiety. High vs. low exposure (≥P75 = 146 pmol/g Hb, vs. Interpretation The findings support an association between prenatal acrylamide exposure and increased incidence of depression and anxiety in adolescence and adulthood. These findings require replication in cohorts with repeated exposure measurements of a range of dietary exposures to establish to what extent the prenatal exposure to acrylamide was responsible for the observed associations. Funding European Research Council, Innovation Fund Denmark, Danish Council for Strategic Research and Stockholm University.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of D-β-hydroxybutyrate ester in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (KETO-ALS)–a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study
abstract: Background Hypermetabolism and weight loss are prominent features of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Here, we sought to target the energy deficit in ALS by applying oral ketone bodies as high-energetic substrates. Methods Patients with probable or definite ALS were enrolled to this randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, double-blind, monocentre phase 2 trial. Eligible patients had a decline of ALS functional rating scale revised (ALSFRS-R) of at least 0.33 points/month. They were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive D-β-hydroxybutyrate ester (βHB, 30 g/day) or placebo. Primary endpoint was change of neurofilament light chain (NfL) per month, measured as slope over 6 months. Multiple linear regressions models were applied to adjust for NfL, age, BMI, and slow vital capacity (SVC) at baseline. The trial is registered with clinicaltrials.gov, number NCT04820478. Findings Between April 5, 2022, and February 12, 2025, 81 patients were randomly assigned to receive βHB (n = 40) or placebo (n = 41) and included in the intention-to-treat analysis. In the unadjusted analysis, the primary endpoint NfL slope was negative, showing a decline of −0.5 pg/mL/month (IQR −3.2 to 2.0, minimum −11.2, maximum 10.4) in the βHB group and a stable course of 0.0 pg/mL/month (IQR −1.7 to 3.3, minimum −6.2, maximum 49.0) in the placebo group (p = 0.094). In the adjusted analysis, the NfL slope showed a benefit for the βHB group (−1.5 pg/ml/month in βHB vs. +2.8 pg/ml/month in placebo, mean difference −4.2 pg/ml/month, 95% CI - ∞ to −1.1, p=0.014). When using a mixed effect model, this effect was not statistically different (−0.4 pg/ml/month in βHB vs. +0.3 pg/ml/month in placebo, mean difference −0.7 pg/ml, month, p=0.30). In the unadjusted analysis, ALSFRS-R showed a faster decline in the verum group (−1.4 points/month (IQR −2.1 to −0.6) vs. −0.8 points/month (IQR −1.2 to −0.2), p=0.020). No significant difference between βHB and placebo was found regarding clinical endpoints such as ALSFRS-R or BMI in the adjusted analysis. βHB was well tolerated, with similar frequency of adverse events across both groups. Interpretation Whether the effects on NfL can be confirmed and translated into meaningful clinical effects, remains to be clarified by a larger phase 3 trial with extended treatment duration. βHB was well tolerated. Funding This was an investigator-initiated study, funded by a private donation.

title: Excess adiposity and early cardiometabolic risk markers among adolescents and young adults in 70 countries: a multi-country cross-sectional study
abstract: Background The recent Lancet Commission recommended moving beyond body mass index (BMI)-only assessment by confirming excess adiposity with waist-based measures or, where available, direct body fat assessment. However, global evidence on the prevalence, classification, and early cardiometabolic relevance of anthropometrically confirmed excess adiposity (hereafter excess adiposity) among adolescents and young adults remains limited. We conducted this study across 70 countries in six World Health Organization (WHO) regions. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we used nationally representative WHO STEPS data from 70 countries between 2010 and 2023. Excess adiposity was defined using a Lancet Commission-informed anthropometric framework incorporating BMI, waist circumference (WC), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR). Random-effects meta-analysis estimated prevalence, and regression models examined associations with cardiometabolic risk markers. Findings Among 60,634 individuals aged 15–29 years, the prevalence of excess adiposity was 33.7% (95% CI 29.4–38.0), ranging from 19.1% in South-East Asia to 48.2% in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Notably, 15.7% of participants had waist-confirmed adiposity, defined by both high WC and WHtR ≥ 0.50, despite not meeting BMI criteria for obesity. Higher odds of excess adiposity were observed in upper-middle-income countries (OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.40–4.60), high-income countries (OR 5.92, 95% CI 3.23–10.8), and physically inactive participants (OR 1.21, 95% CI 1.14–1.29). Excess adiposity was also associated with higher odds of having at least one (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.86–2.49) and multiple (OR 4.09, 95% CI 3.20–5.23) cardiometabolic risk markers. Interpretation This study found that nearly one-third of adolescents and young adults had excess adiposity. Notably, one in six participants had waist-confirmed adiposity despite not meeting BMI criteria for obesity, identifying a group with greater cardiometabolic risk burden that would be missed by BMI alone. These findings support the Lancet Commission's move beyond BMI-only assessment and highlight the need to include waist-based measures in surveillance and prevention strategies to identify adiposity-related cardiometabolic risk earlier. Funding None.

title: Innovation in medical surge capacity during the 2026 Venezuela earthquake response: operationalising a Specialised Care Team for Emergency Remote Clinical Support
abstract: Adaptability is a hallmark of disaster response. A first-time innovation within the Emergency Medical Team (EMT) framework was developed as part of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)-supported response to the 2026 Venezuelan earthquakes: the operationalisation of a Specialised Care Team for Emergency Remote Clinical Support (SCT-ERCS). This initiative, now formalised as a framework agreement between PAHO and the Panamerican Trauma Society, holds promise for expanding remote medical consultation in future disasters (Fig.

title: Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial
abstract: Background Long-term data for digital therapeutics in urinary incontinence are scarce. We assessed whether improvements with app-based multimodal therapy are sustained over 48 weeks, and outcomes after a 12-week delay in initiation. Methods In this prespecified 48-week follow-up of the DINKS (Digital Incontinence Study) randomised waitlist-controlled trial, women (≥18 years) with stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence recruited between April 30 and September 2 2024 across Germany received app-based therapy immediately or after a 12-week waitlist, alongside standard care. The primary outcome was change from baseline in ICIQ-UI-SF (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire–Urinary Incontinence Short Form) score at weeks 12, 24, 36, and 48. Trial registration: NCT06389838. Findings Data availability declined progressively from 186 of 194 participants (95.9%) at week 12–66 (34.0%) at week 48. Pooled improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference at 12, 24, and 36 weeks after therapy start (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks −4.13, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) −4.80 to −3.47), and 73–77% of participants met the responder threshold. Differences between immediate and delayed initiation were small (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks 0.08, −1.09 to 1.25). The week-48 estimate (−3.88, −4.74 to −3.03) was intervention-group only, from 27 of 96. No adverse events were reported. Interpretation App-based multimodal therapy was associated with clinically meaningful improvements sustained through at least 36 weeks after intervention start. Differences between immediate and 12-week-delayed initiation were small relative to the minimal important difference, but no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and only one delay was tested; symptoms were unchanged while waiting, so waiting times should still be minimised. Confirmation in larger trials with active comparators is needed. Funding Kranus Health GmbH.

title: Predicting PANSS symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorders using speech only: an international, multi-centre, computational secondary analysis across multiple languages
abstract: Background Speech carries cues to variation in mental state in schizophrenia, typically indexed with clinician-rated scales such as Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS). In this study, we aggregate multi-centre recordings to assemble a large corpus and assess symptom-prediction models at scale, to enable rater-independent, efficient, and reproducible assessments for early detection of relapse-related signals from speech. Methods In this computational secondary analysis, we compiled data from 453 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders, recruited between 2005 and 2026 from ten global sites in the Czech Republic, United States, Spain, Chile, France, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Türkiye, Germany, and China, and clipped their speech recordings into 6664 segments. Across three featuresets, acoustic-prosodic profile, pretrained multilingual embeddings, and their concatenation, we compared 16 algorithms in separate item-specific models to predict eight relapse-related PANSS items, including three positive (P1, P2, P3), three negative (N1, N4, N6), and two general (G5, G9) items, on speaker-disjoint splits. Performance was assessed by root-mean-squared-error (RMSE) at both segment and participant (median-aggregation) levels. Best model per item underwent bias checks for age, sex, education, and symptom severity. Findings Best-performing models predicted symptoms with prediction errors of 1.5 or lower: P1 1.544/1.527, P2 1.318/1.107, P3 1.487/1.542, N1 1.071/1.030, N4 1.521/1.430, N6 0.869/0.855, G5 0.951/0.882, G9 1.298/1.282 (segment/participant). Performance of pretrained embeddings surpassed acoustic-prosodic features and concatenation. Results were comparable in languages or language variants with fewer available speech and language computational resources. We found no bias by age, sex, or education, aside from reduced N4 accuracy in males; but performance degraded with higher symptom severity. Interpretation Speech can support automatic assessment of schizophrenia symptoms using pretrained embeddings, even without transcripts. Such models show promise as clinically meaningful, efficient, and low-burden tools for real-time monitoring of symptom trajectories. Future work should validate these models prospectively in higher-severity samples and improve clinical interpretability. Funding European Union Horizon.

title: Brain injury after single fetal demise in monochorionic twin pregnancies: an international multicentre retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Single fetal demise (sFD) in monochorionic (MC) twins may lead to acute exsanguination through placental anastomoses and result in brain injury in initially surviving cotwins. We aimed to evaluate the prevalence, type, severity, and factors associated with brain injury in initially surviving cotwins after sFD. Methods In this international multicentre retrospective cohort study, all MC twin pregnancies complicated by sFD between 1 January 2000 and 1 January 2025 at 13 fetal therapy centres in Argentina, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Israel, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom were included. Pregnancies with sFD following laser surgery, selective feticide or twin anaemia-polycythaemia sequence were excluded. The primary outcome was severe brain injury in the initially surviving cotwin, assessed using all available fetal and/or neonatal neuroimaging. Severe brain injury was defined as cystic periventricular leukomalacia, multicystic encephalomalacia, migration disorders, severe ventriculomegaly or volume loss, acute hypoxic-ischaemic injury, arterial ischaemic infarction, high-grade intraventricular haemorrhage, non-punctate intraparenchymal or cerebellar haemorrhage. Findings A total of 395 MC pregnancies with sFD and available neuroimaging were included. Median gestational age at diagnosis of sFD was 22.7 (interquartile range [IQR] 19.3–27.1) weeks. Severe brain injury was detected in 18% (72/395) of initially surviving cotwins. The most common type was multicystic encephalomalacia in 32% (23/72). The presumed timing of severe brain injury was antenatal in 82% (59/72), perinatal in 5% (4/72), postnatal in 10% (7/72) and indeterminate in 3% (2/72) of cases. In multivariable analysis, later gestational age at sFD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.09 per week, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03–1.14; p=0.001) and fetal anaemia (aOR 2.29, 95% CI 1.24–4.25; p=0.009) were associated with severe brain injury. In liveborn infants, earlier gestational age at birth was associated with severe brain injury (p = 0.009). Interpretation Severe brain injury was diagnosed in one fifth of initially surviving cotwins in MC twin pregnancies after sFD and occurred predominantly antenatally, with imaging patterns consistent with hypoxic-ischaemic injury following acute exsanguination. Our findings support routine serial antenatal and postnatal neuroimaging after sFD. Earlier birth was associated with brain injury, but causality cannot be inferred because of confounding by indication. sFD alone should not prompt early delivery in clinically stable pregnancies. Prospective studies are needed to determine the optimal timing and modality of neuroimaging after sFD and evaluate management strategies including the use of intrauterine transfusion and optimal timing of delivery. Funding European Society for Paediatric Research (ESPR), Leids Universitair Fonds (LUF), and Gratama Stichting, Strong Babies, Honors College Leiden University Medical Center, Janivo Stichting, Gisela Thier Fonds, Raynor Cerebellar Initiatives and Vaillant Stichting.

title: Comparative effectiveness of lipid-lowering therapies for primary cardiovascular prevention: a network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
abstract: Background Comparative effectiveness across lipid-lowering drug classes in primary prevention remains uncertain. Methods We conducted a random-effects network meta-analysis of randomised trials of lipid-lowering therapy in adults without a prior coronary event, stratified by baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from inception to July 25, 2026; included trials were published 1984–2026. Statin-containing regimens were classified by intensity, with no lipid-lowering therapy as reference. Findings 29 trials (218,657 unique participants) were included; hazard ratios are shown with 95% CIs. At high ASCVD risk, evolocumab plus statin (0.59, 0.49–0.71), bempedoic acid (0.64, 0.48–0.85) and high-intensity statin (0.80, 0.69–0.92) reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) vs. no lipid-lowering therapy. Against its statin comparator, evolocumab retained benefit (0.74, 0.65–0.83), whereas eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) (0.81, 0.62–1.06) and fibrates (4-point MACE, low-to-moderate risk; 1.04, 0.80–1.36) did not. At low-to-moderate risk, benefit was graded by statin intensity (high 0.53, 0.37–0.75; moderate 0.76, 0.64–0.91); for 4-point MACE, ezetimibe (0.66, 0.50–0.87) and fibrates (0.81, 0.70–0.94) also reduced events. Heterogeneity was moderate in the 2-point and 3-point networks (I 2 59–62%) and no network contained a closed loop, precluding consistency testing. Two trials were at high risk of bias; certainty was low or very low for 23 of 27 comparisons. No comparison contained enough trials to test for small-study effects. Interpretation Benefit in primary prevention tracked statin intensity rather than drug class. Evolocumab added to a statin conferred further benefit over that statin, whereas EPA and fibrates did not, and bempedoic acid is an option where statins are not tolerated. Funding None.

title: Effectiveness, safety and therapeutic potential of medical cannabis across treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Medical cannabis has been suggested to have a therapeutic role in selected treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. We analyzed the available evidence to assess the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Methods For this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, EBSCO, and PubMed for studies published between January 1, 1970, and April 25, 2026. We considered studies examining any type or formulation of medical cannabis in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Primary outcomes were disorder-specific clinical improvement measures. Safety outcomes were adverse events, serious adverse events, and withdrawals due to adverse events. Evidence from studies was synthesized as equivalent odds ratios (eORs) for comparative outcomes and as pooled proportions for single-arm safety outcomes, via random-effects meta-analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, and structured quality assessment for case series and case reports, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251148868. Findings 127 eligible studies were included, of which 32 studies involving 3645 participants contributed to meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed improvement in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34–0.72), refractory pain (eOR = 0.48, 95% CI=0.30–0.78), and refractory multiple sclerosis spasticity (eOR = 0.22, 95% CI=0.07–0.75). Evidence for psychiatric disorders was scarce. Small randomized trials reported improvement in PTSD-related nightmares and cannabis dependence after failed cessation. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in hyperarousal, residual obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and refractory Tourette syndrome. Findings for treatment-resistant anxiety were inconsistent, and schizophrenia did not show a reliable therapeutic effect. Controlled analyses showed higher odds of any adverse events in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR = 2.22, 95% CI=1.52–3.23) and refractory multiple sclerosis (eOR = 1.89, 95% CI=1.01–3.52), with higher odds of serious adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events also observed in drug-resistant epilepsy. In single-arm and real-world studies, pooled proportions of any adverse events ranged from 15.5% in multiple sclerosis to 66.0% in Tourette syndrome, with substantial heterogeneity. Interpretation Adjunctive pharmaceutical cannabidiol has the most consistent comparative evidence for reducing seizure frequency in selected drug-resistant epilepsy. Evidence for refractory pain and multiple sclerosis is heterogeneous and varies by clinical indication, cannabinoid formulation, and outcome definition. Evidence in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders remains limited and is insufficient to support routine clinical recommendations. Further high-quality studies directly examining diagnosis-specific and formulation-specific effects, safety, and tolerability are needed. Funding STI2030-Major Projects and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

title: Early best available antibiotic therapy for multidrug-resistant gram-negative bloodstream infections: a target trial emulation
abstract: Background The effect of timely appropriate antibiotics in multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB) bloodstream infections (BSIs) remains uncertain. Robust evidence is needed to inform diagnostic and treatment strategies, especially across settings with high antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and varying access to effective preventive and treatment therapeutics. Methods Using data from the prospective ACORN-HAI cohort across 19 Asian countries between September 2022 and February 2025, we emulated a target trial comparing early guideline-recommended best available therapy (BAT) initiated within 24 h of blood culture collection (early BAT), versus no early BAT among adults with monomicrobial BSIs due to third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCRE), carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), or carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter spp. (CRA). Confounding was addressed using inverse probability weighting. The primary outcome was 14-day all-cause mortality. Whether mortality benefit differed according to disease severity was assessed using relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Findings Among 1412 adults (706 3GCRE, 442 CRE, and 264 CRA BSIs), early BAT was associated with lower 14-day mortality (18.5% versus 25.6% without early BAT; risk difference [RD] −7.1%; 95% CI −11.3%, −3.0%). In 3GCRE BSIs, the mortality reduction was 7.4% (RD −7.4%; 95% CI −12.2, −2.5). Among carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CR-GNB) BSIs, where early BAT predominantly consisted of polymyxin-based regimens (81.7%, 147/180), the estimated RDs were −3.3% (95% CI −13.8, 10.4) for CRE and −7.5% (95% CI −19.1, 4.0) for CRA. Interaction analyses showed a greater mortality benefit of early BAT in severe 3GCRE infections (RERI 2.06, 95% CI 0.47, 4.41), but not in CR-GNB BSIs. Interpretation Early BAT was associated with reduced mortality in MDR-GNB BSIs overall. By pathogen group, a mortality reduction was observed in 3GCRE BSIs, whereas findings for CR-GNB BSIs were uncertain. In the context of predominantly polymyxin-based therapy, reducing treatment delays alone may therefore be insufficient to improve outcomes in CR-GNB BSIs, highlighting the need to develop and optimise prevention and therapeutic strategies, especially across AMR-prevalent settings. Funding Wellcome Trust, National University of Singapore, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, Duke-NUS Medical School, Nanyang Technological University (Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine), Singapore National Centre for Infectious Diseases, and Singapore Medical Research Council.

title: Single-dose/day versus extended antibiotic prophylaxis for elective urological surgery: a prospective randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Excess and prolonged antibiotic use for perioperative prophylaxis is a very common clinical practice. This overuse is largely driven by ingrained protocols rooted in fear of postoperative infection, despite limited evidence supporting extended prophylaxis. The objective was to evaluate whether extending antibiotic prophylaxis beyond the immediate perioperative period provides additional protection against postoperative symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients undergoing elective urological surgery. Methods This open-label, randomized controlled trial included patients scheduled for elective urological surgery from March 2024 to September 2025. The patients were randomized 1:1 to either single-dose or extended perioperative prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was symptomatic urinary tract infection (sUTI) within 30 days of surgery. Secondary endpoints included one-week sUTI rate, asymptomatic bacteriuria at 7 and 30 days, 30-day hospital readmission, antibiotic escalation, length of stay and subgroup analyses by age, co-morbidity, surgical approach, and procedure type. The trial was prospectively registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2024/03/063953). Findings A total of 334 patients completed follow-up and were included in the analysis (single-dose group: n=169; extended-prophylaxis group: n=165). The 30-day sUTI rate was 7.1% (12/169) in single versus 5.5% (9/165) in extended prophylaxis groups (Absolute risk difference 1.6%, 95% CI: −3.6% to 6.8%; p=0.536). All secondary outcome parameters were comparable between the groups with no statistically significant difference. No patient in either group developed septic shock or infection-related mortality. Interpretation As a test of difference, without implying equivalence or non-inferiority, there was no statistically significant difference in postoperative symptomatic UTI incidence between single-dose and extended antibiotic prophylaxis for elective urological surgery. Funding None.

title: Home-based transfusions in hospice patients with hematologic malignancies: a pilot study
abstract: Background Hospice care (HC) for patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) is underutilized due to concerns about cessation of blood transfusions. Home-based transfusion (HBT) programs have proven to be safe, but little research exists for HM patients in HC. We hypothesized that HBT protocol could be safely implemented to reduce symptoms burden, lengthen life expectancy and improve quality of life in HC. Methods In a non-randomized pilot study between 8/2020 and 7/2023, adult transfusion-dependent HM patients were offered weekly transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and/or one unit of platelets based on symptoms criteria, not lab values. Exclusion criteria included prior transfusion reactions, extended blood typing, or residence outside 50 miles from the transfusion center. Hospice agencies provided management and support, while Our Blood Institute (OBI) provided palliative HBT. Symptom scores and complete blood counts (CBC) were collected weekly, and EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life (QOL) questionnaire was completed before and after transfusions. The primary feasibility and safety outcomes were recruitment, ability to administer indicated transfusions, and transfusion reactions. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04454723) on 6/30/2020. Findings We enrolled 21 patients (mean age in years=67.1 (standard deviation (SD) = 14.4); 100% enrollment, one withdrew consent). Participants received an average of 3.4 units (SD = 3.4) of platelets or PRBCs. No transfusion reactions reported. Mean cost was $571 per week (SD = $939). The EORTC Composite Score least squares-mean difference (post-pre- transfusion) increased 0.18 (SE = 1.88) (p-value = 0.92) but not significantly. Median hospice duration was 11 days, IQR=8–40 days, 95% CI: 9–33 days. All patients died at home, with no hospitalizations or intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. Interpretation HBT, in the setting of hospice represents a feasible and safe option for further study to avoid costly hospitalizations and ICU admissions, with limited cost. This trial demonstrates proof of concept for an economical, patient-centered HBT protocol in HM patients receiving HC. Funding P30CA225520, TSET.

title: Efficacy and safety of duloxetine for osteoarthritis: a comparator-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Duloxetine is recommended for osteoarthritis pain, yet its role relative to placebo, active pharmacological comparators, and add-on therapy remains uncertain. We assessed the efficacy and safety of duloxetine for osteoarthritis using a comparator-stratified meta-analysis. Methods We searched major English and Chinese databases from inception to August 30, 2026, for randomised controlled trials of duloxetine in adults with osteoarthritis. Eligible trials compared duloxetine with placebo, active pharmacological treatments, or add-on/background therapy controls. Pain and physical function were the primary outcomes. We used random-effects meta-analysis, comparator-stratified and duration-based subgroup analyses, meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) certainty assessment. Findings 20 studies, contributing 21 eligible randomised comparisons and 3455 participants, were included. Duloxetine was associated with reduced Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain (standardised mean difference −0.36, 95% CI −0.58 to −0.14) and improved physical function (−0.41, −0.58 to −0.25), but with more adverse events overall (risk ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.79). Comparator-stratified analyses were conducted separately for placebo-controlled, active-comparator, and add-on/background-therapy settings, which addressed distinct clinical questions. Placebo-controlled studies provided the clearest evidence of benefit, whereas duloxetine did not show clear superiority over active pharmacological comparators. Add-on or combination-therapy estimates for pain and function were inconclusive: the confidence intervals crossed the null and the certainty of evidence was very low. No statistically significant associations were detected between maintenance dose, treatment duration, or study quality and WOMAC treatment effects; however, these exploratory analyses were based on a limited number of studies. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high; evidence was low for WOMAC pain and total scores, and overall adverse events, and moderate for WOMAC physical function, stiffness. Interpretation Duloxetine was associated with improvements in pain and physical function in osteoarthritis, with the clearest benefit observed versus placebo. Evidence from active-comparator and add-on/background-therapy studies was limited, heterogeneous, and inconclusive; these analyses did not establish superiority over active treatment or a consistent additive treatment effect. Duloxetine may be considered a conditional pharmacological option for osteoarthritis pain management, particularly when non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are unsuitable; however, its comparative benefit over active treatments remains uncertain. Funding Shaanxi Postdoctoral Research Program, Natural Science Basic Research Program of Shaanxi, Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities, China Postdoctoral Science Foundation, and NHMRC Investigator Grant.

title: An explainable artificial intelligence system for prognostic assessment and decision support in diabetic foot ulcer care: a multicentre derivation and validation study with prospective randomised evaluation
abstract: Background Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) carry risks of recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality, but most prediction models address single outcomes and have limited interpretability. We developed an interpretable multi-outcome machine-learning framework for individualised DFU risk assessment and prospective clinical evaluation. Methods We conducted a development and validation study across three hospitals in China from January 1, 2018, to April 30, 2025. We used electronic medical records and follow-up data from 763 patients at Centres A and B to develop and internally validate an ensemble of single-task extreme gradient boosting (ST-XGBoost) and single-task multilayer perceptron (ST-MLP) models to predict cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality. The locked ensemble was externally validated in 100 patients at Centre C. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, with interpretability evaluated using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). From January 5 to March 5, 2026, we performed a prospective comparative evaluation. We randomised 202 participants (1:1) to usual care or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted care, of whom 200 were analysed. We compared AI-assisted physician decision-making via an evolvable web-based online prediction platform versus usual care. The outcome was overall quality score of the final clinical recommendation. The platform supports follow-up data collection for future offline model updating. Findings In the training dataset, cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality occurred in 638, 208, 226, and 167 patients, respectively; the corresponding numbers in the external validation dataset were 80, 34, 24, and 25. In independent external validation, the ST-XGBoost + ST-MLP ensemble outperformed six comparators, with a macro-averaged AUC of 0.901, accuracy of 0.875, and F1 score of 0.830. Outcome-specific discrimination was highest for amputation (AUC 0.953) and all-cause mortality (AUC 0.951), followed by cure (AUC 0.880) and recurrence (AUC 0.820). In the prospective evaluation, AI-assisted recommendations received higher scores than corresponding clinician recommendations (7.77 vs 6.47; mean difference 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08–1.52; p < 0.0001), with the largest gain in completeness. The AI-assisted group showed better short-term follow-up engagement and glucose-management adherence. Interpretation We demonstrate that integrating gradient-boosted trees and neural networks enables explainable prediction of complex DFU trajectories and may support prioritised, individualised clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, recurrence estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Funding Xuzhou Municipal Health Commission Science and Technology Project (XWYHT20240128).

title: A review of global health architecture reform efforts—navigating between reform and fragmentation
abstract: A multitude of initiatives addressing global health architecture reform have materialized following the rapid changes in official development assistance in 2025. There is widespread agreement that an overhaul is vital alongside a realignment towards country-led priority-setting. However, the myriad initiatives may result in replicating the failed architecture of the past through again reinforcing donor-led agendas, duplication of efforts, top-down approaches and fragmentation. In response to this, we aimed to map 11 key initiatives of global health architecture reform through predefined categories, addressing domains, mechanisms, thematic areas, governance and financing. The 11 initiatives included are: Accra Reset; Africa CDC Health Security and Sovereignty Initiative; European Donor Alignment; Gavi Leap; Health Works Leaders Coalition; HEAR CSO Consortium; Lusaka Agenda; Sevilla Platform of Action; US Bilateral Health Agreements; WHO Global Health Architecture Reform Process; Wellcome Trust Convening Dialogues. Applying a comparative analysis, we identified key areas of consensus, duplication, fragmentation, gaps and emerging themes. To help further understanding, we share details of the current experience in Uganda with a focus on financing as a case-study. We find that most initiatives target shaping alignment/efficiency or financing/funding as primary domains, while capacity building is largely missing. This creates a disconnect between reform ambitions and capacity to deliver. While governance is intrinsic to any architecture reform, we found diverse approaches leading to unclear governance and accountability overall. Further, while financing and funding underpins any capacity for realistic reform and progress, there is a lack of concrete detail on how increased fiscal space and such capacity will be created nor a strong acknowledgment of the need for increased financing amid ongoing cuts. We conclude by highlighting critical outstanding questions to further guide the reform process, including design, governance, mandates, financing, milestones, financing, and accountability.

title: CT-based AI risk support for cystic renal masses: multicenter validation, reader study, and a randomized implementation study
abstract: Background Cystic renal masses are frequently overtreated. We developed and evaluated the Kidney Imaging-based Triage Engine for Cystic Renal Masses (KITE-CRM), a computed tomography (CT)-based deep-learning pathway using artificial intelligence (AI) to support malignancy risk assessment in cystic renal masses (CRMs). Methods We conducted a multicentre development and validation study in China. In phase 1 (January 2020–December 2021), we developed the system in a retrospective training cohort from a tertiary referral center. CRMs were defined as renal lesions with predominantly cystic features. Corticomedullary-phase contrast-enhanced CT was the sole model input. In phase 2 (January 2022–October 2025), we externally validated the model across five independent hospitals. The core task was lesion-level malignancy discrimination; secondary tasks classified malignant lesions as clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) versus other malignant subtypes and stratified ccRCC as high-grade versus low-grade disease. Retrospective cohorts comprised 3150 patients. The core task used 570 training cases (142 malignant), 235 internal-validation cases (137 malignant), and 528 external cases (160 malignant). Three-dimensional processing used one index lesion per patient and a fixed threshold of 0.586442888. In a randomized crossover multi-reader, multi-case study, six radiologists interpreted 117 external-cohort cases with and without AI; outcomes were area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, specificity, reading time, and user acceptance. In phase 3 (November 2025–February 2026), 5869 eligible consecutive adults undergoing contrast-enhanced abdominal CT at Changhai Hospital were randomized 1:1 to AI-assisted (n = 2934) or standard reporting (n = 2935). The primary clinical endpoint was the proportion of pathologically benign lesions among treated lesions. The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500112290); model code is publicly available. Findings Internal-validation AUROC was 0.996 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.990–0.999) and Brier score 0.046 (0.036–0.058). External AUROCs were 0.913–0.999, excluding Test 4 (AUROC 1.000; three malignant cases). External sensitivity ranged from 19/24 (79.2%) to 3/3 (100.0%) and specificity from 100/116 (86.2%) to 33/33 and 115/115 (100.0%). AI assistance increased reader-averaged AUROC from 0.825 to 0.973 (difference, 0.149; 95% CI, 0.091–0.206) and reduced mean interpretation time from 9.7 to 5.5 min. Benign pathology occurred in 28/171 (16.4%) treated lesions with AI versus 104/258 (40.3%) with standard care (difference, −23.9 percentage points; 95% CI, −31.7 to −15.4). The treated AI-evaluable CRM subgroup difference was non-significant (5/29 [17.2%] versus 19/56 [33.9%]; p=0.105). In post hoc intention-to-treat analysis, benign intervention occurred in 28/2934 (0.95%) versus 104/2935 (3.54%) randomized participants (risk difference, −2.59 percentage points; 95% CI, −3.38 to −1.85; p < 0.0001). Median reporting time was 7.6 versus 18.5 min. Interpretation KITE-CRM improved assisted interpretation and reporting efficiency. Management findings do not establish long-term oncologic safety or CRM-specific clinical superiority. The model complements, rather than replaces, Bosniak assessment, indicated multiphase CT or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and clinical judgment. Broader prospective evaluation is needed. Funding National Natural Science Foundation of China and Shanghai municipal research programmes.

title: ESMO Congress 2026
Sepsis-related hospitalisation risk in preterm-born and term-born children and adolescents: a nationwide registry study
abstract: Background: The burden of severe infections in children remains inadequately characterised. Preterm birth is a risk factor for neonatal sepsis, yet whether this risk persists beyond the neonatal period is unclear. We examined the risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation during childhood and adolescence in term-born and preterm-born children. Methods: Norwegian nationwide birth registry data (1992–2021) were linked with hospital discharge data (2008–2021). Using a standardised definition, sepsis-related hospitalisations were classified as explicit (sepsis diagnosis code) or implicit (infection plus organ dysfunction diagnosis codes). We estimated rate ratios (RRs) using adjusted negative binomial regression and sibling-controlled odds ratios (ORs) using conditional logistic regression by completed weeks of gestation (23–27, 28–31, 32–33, 34–36, 37–38, and 39–41 weeks), stratified by age (3–11 months, 1–5 years, and 6–15 years). Findings: Following 1,672,442 births, 12,932 sepsis episodes were available in the data. Hospitalisation rates for sepsis-related admissions were highest during infancy (23–27 weeks gestation: 75·4 [95% confidence interval (CI) 55·2–95·7], 39–41 weeks: 3·2 [95% CI 3·0–3·4] per 1000 person-years at ages 3–11 months). Compared with term-born, rates of sepsis-related hospitalisations increased by lower gestational age groups in both population and sibling analyses. Comparing extremely preterm versus term-born children, RRs were 23·4 (95% CI 17·7–30·9) at ages 3–11 months, 19·7 (14·7–26·5) at ages 1–5 years, and 4·6 (2·1–10·3) at ages 6–15 years. Sibling ORs were 23·8 (10·5–54·3), 28·9 (11·1–75·6), and 3·8 (1·5–9·8), respectively. Interpretation: Lower gestational age was robustly associated with an increased risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation throughout childhood and adolescence, supporting that low gestational age at birth should be recognised as a persistent risk factor for severe infections beyond the neonatal period.

title: Incidence of heavy menstrual bleeding and prevalence of co-occurring conditions from seven countries across Europe and North America: an EHDEN real-world data study
abstract: Background Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) presents a significant burden for women but is often under-diagnosed and its consequences under-recognised. Improved real-world characterisation of HMB may help identify unmet needs and support earlier and more accurate diagnosis. This study aimed to estimate HMB incidence and prevalence of co-occurring conditions. Methods EHDEN HMB was an observational cohort study of nine real-world data sources from seven countries across Europe and North America covering different healthcare settings (primary care-only, hospital-only, primary/specialist non-hospital, all). The study period was from Jan 1, 2000 (or the earliest available date thereafter) to the end of data availability (2021–2024 depending on the data source). Overall and annual incidence rates (IRs) of HMB, as well as the prevalence of co-occurring conditions during the year pre- and post-index (i.e., first HMB diagnosis), were assessed among women aged 11–55 years. Findings A total of 3,797,918 women with HMB were included. Overall IR ranged from 0.7 to 25.9 per 1000 person-years, with highest rates observed in data sources encompassing all healthcare settings and lowest in primary care- or hospital-only data. IRs were also highest in women aged 30–44. Pain, anaemia, and dysmenorrhoea were the most common co-occurring conditions both pre-index and post-index (ranging from 5.5% to 21.0% pre-index vs 3.0% to 8.9% post-index for general pain, 3.2% to 20.9% vs 2.0% to 7.0% for narrow/gynaecological pain, 3.4% to 11.5% vs 1.9% to 5.7% for anaemia, and 0.7% to 13.6% vs 0.5% to 5.5% for dysmenorrhoea). Uterine leiomyoma, a diagnosed condition considered to underlie HMB, was also common both pre-index (0.9% to 10.5%) and post-index (1.1% to 9.1%). Interpretation To our knowledge, this was the first large-scale real-world study characterising HMB. IR and prevalence of co-occurring conditions varied substantially across healthcare settings and data sources. Changes in prevalence of co-occurring conditions pre- and post-index may reflect changes in clinical management following an HMB diagnosis. Greater awareness of HMB and related conditions may support improved screening and earlier diagnoses, ultimately improving patient outcomes and quality of life. Funding Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking (no. 806968) with support from European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme and EFPIA; Norwegian Research Council (no. 31270).

title: Efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with toripalimab in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a phase II trial and biological correlate analysis
abstract: Background Two prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trials of locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) suggest that reduced-volume radiotherapy, delivering a full dose only to residual tumors following induction chemotherapy (IC), can achieve comparable efficacy with reduced toxicity. However, only 10.0% of patients achieved a complete response (CR) following IC with gemcitabine and cisplatin. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy with 3 cycles of toripalimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin. Methods We conducted a single-arm phase II trial at a single center in China. We included patients aged 18–65 years with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed, stage III-IVA NPC. Participants received 3 cycles of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy, with toripalimab (240 mg on day 1), gemcitabine (1 g/m2 on days 1 and 8) and cisplatin (80 mg/m2 on day 1) once every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was CR. Secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRRFS), and safety. Tumor response was assessed 1 week after the completion of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. Exploratory endpoints were comprehensive marker analysis using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05813626). Findings Between April 21, 2023 and August 15, 2025, 94 patients were screened and 91 patients were enrolled. At last follow-up (March 16, 2026), the median (interquartile range [IQR]) follow-up time was 24.3 (13.0–30.6) months. The intention-to-treat analysis showed that CR was observed in 30 patients [33.0% (95% CI: 26.4–47.0)]. The 2-year LRRFS, DMFS, and OS rates were 97.1% (95% CI: 93.3–100.0), 94.8% (95% CI: 89.3–100.0), and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.9–100.0), respectively. Grade 3 and 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 36 (39.6%) and 10 (11.0%) of 91 patients, respectively. Integrating scRNA-seq, mIHC, and biological correlatives, we identify CD44-mediated regulation of Treg abundance as a critical determinant of response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. Interpretation Neoadjuvant toripalimab plus chemotherapy achieved promising efficacy with manageable toxicity. scRNA-seq uncovered immune heterogeneity underlying treatment response, informing precision neoadjuvant therapy for NPC. Funding This study was funded by the Natural Science Foundation of Zhejiang Province (No. TGY24H160081).

title: Corrigendum to ‘A brief video intervention targeting self-stigma among childhood maltreatment survivors: an international, multicentre, single-blind, randomised controlled trial’ eClinicalMedicine, volume 100 (2026), 104201
abstract: The authors regret to inform we have identified an error in the published ethics statement concerning the Swedish part of the study. The study did receive ethical approval in Sweden, but this information was inadvertently omitted/misstated in the published article.
